intent: Bring config.sh under the 250-line cap without changing the policy it defines, and replace the brief's prescribed safety net — which does not work — with one that does.
scope: phone_focus_mode/config_paths.sh, config_dns.sh, config_curfew.sh, config_tether.sh, config_launcher.sh - new siblings
phone_focus_mode/docs/policy-lists.md - new: the rationale prose moved out of config.sh
phone_focus_mode/deploy.sh - all five siblings added to both hardcoded lists
phone_focus_mode/lib/tests/daemon_cases_status.sh - new: split out so daemon_cases_state.sh stays under the cap
Non-goal: changing any list, threshold, interval or path value.
changes: THE BRIEF'S FINGERPRINT RECIPE IS BROKEN AND WAS REPLACED. It prescribes load_policy + dataclasses.asdict + json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, default=str) + sha256, with baseline 1624750c…. Four policy fields are frozenset, which json cannot encode, so default=str stringifies each in SET ITERATION ORDER — which depends on PYTHONHASHSEED and is therefore random per process. Measured: three consecutive runs produced three different digests, so the recipe can never match any recorded baseline and would flag every split as a regression. Pinning PYTHONHASHSEED=0 produced one stable digest, confirming the cause.

The repo already contains a deterministic serializer: python3 -m python_pkg.focus_policy. Before relying on it, its completeness was checked against dataclasses.asdict recursively — it emits all 16 dataclass fields plus 6 more (schema_version, always_blocked_packages, blockable_system_packages, always_on_vpn_package, private_dns_host, vpn_lockdown). It is strictly stronger than the brief's method, not a weaker proxy, so it is the fingerprint used here. Baseline 83e05e82….

Audited the loader BEFORE extracting. python_pkg/focus_policy/loader.py builds the policy by running a regex over the text of config.sh alone (plus a sibling config_secrets.sh). Fifteen variables are therefore pinned to config.sh; moving any of them would not raise an error, it would silently yield an empty set — which for WHITELIST reads as 'nothing is allowed'. That list is documented at the top of config.sh and in config_paths.sh.

Extractions are variable-scoped, not line-range. An initial line-range attempt cut through the middle of the WHITELIST string, leaving an unterminated quote; config.sh then failed to parse and 15 variables vanished from the environment — while the fingerprint still matched, because the loader's regex tolerated it. Reverted and redone with a helper that takes each variable from its assignment through the line closing its quote.

STATE_DIR moved into config_paths.sh rather than staying behind: every path in that file is built from it, and leaving it in config.sh after the source line produced paths like /status.json instead of /data/local/tmp/focus_mode/status.json. Caught by the environment diff, not the fingerprint.

Long rationale prose moved to docs/policy-lists.md with pointers left in place, including the two blocks inside the WHITELIST/NIGHT_WHITELIST strings. The loader and the shell both ignore '#' lines there, and the parsed lists were compared entry-by-entry to confirm it.

verification.evidence: 83e05e82dd1683e1dff1c79a96fec0a4a56aa73295604c681ae355b40a590ba3 before the split and after every one of the six extractions. The loader sees an identical policy.

verification.command: completeness check of policy_to_json against dataclasses.asdict, recursive over nested dicts
verification.evidence: 16 dataclass fields, 22 exported fields, ZERO missing. The exporter is lossless, so its hash cannot be blind to a field the split might mangle.

verification.command: determinism check of the brief's prescribed recipe
verification.evidence: Three runs gave 81e3a371…, 6f4595ce…, cfde0d59… — all different. With PYTHONHASHSEED=0 pinned, two runs gave the same 5f86c8ff…. The nondeterminism is the four frozenset fields being stringified in iteration order. This is why the brief's baseline could never be reproduced.

verification.command: diff of the sourced shell environment against the pre-split commit, in a clean worktree
verification.evidence: 79 variables on both sides, byte-identical. This is the check the fingerprint cannot do: it caught the STATE_DIR ordering bug, where paths expanded against an empty prefix while the policy hash stayed green.

verification.command: entry-by-entry comparison of every parsed package list, comments and blanks stripped as the daemon strips them
verification.evidence: WHITELIST 29, NIGHT_WHITELIST 16, SYSTEM_NEVER_DISABLE 46, ALLOWED_PREFIXES 1, NIGHT_ALLOWED_PREFIXES 1, BROWSER_PACKAGES 2, WORKOUT_UNBLOCK_DOMAINS 15 — all identical. Only comment prose moved.

verification.command: bash -n and sh -n on config.sh and all five siblings
verification.evidence: All parse. The failed line-range attempt was caught by exactly this check reporting 'unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote'.

verification.command: timeout 30 bash phone_focus_mode/deploy.sh; timeout 60 bash phone_focus_mode/run_phone.sh --help
verification.evidence: deploy.sh reaches its usage message, proving it still sources the whole config chain from the checkout. run_phone.sh --help exits 0.
dns_iptables 24, monitor 82, tether_enforcer 17, curfew_net 41, hosts_libs 69, daemon_libs 108, backup_capture 22, adb_common 10, adb_trusted 6 — 379 assertions, 0 failures.

verification.command: systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=2G -p MemorySwapMax=0 python3 -m pytest python_pkg/focus_policy -q
verification.evidence: 137 passed. The reported coverage failure is the repo-wide 100% gate applied to a single-package run, not a regression.

verification.command: deploy-list parity in both directions; shellcheck on each touched file
verification.evidence: 10 new entries (5 push + 5 cp), comm returns empty both ways, and all eight touched shell files are clean standalone.
17 over-cap files, down from 18. config.sh is exactly 250, and the five siblings are 29-118.

risks: config.sh is at exactly 250 lines — the cap, with no headroom. The next comment added to it puts it back over, and the loader-pinned content alone is 184 lines, so there is little room to recover without moving more prose to docs.

The fifteen pinned variables are enforced only by a comment. Nothing mechanically prevents a future edit from moving WHITELIST into a sibling, and the failure would be silent: an empty allowlist parses fine and reads as 'hide everything'. The fingerprint catches it, but only if someone runs it.
UNVERIFIED ON DEVICE, and this one has the largest blast radius of the session: every phone script sources config.sh. If any of the five siblings fails to reach the device, nothing starts at all.

Rationale that used to sit beside the values now lives in docs/policy-lists.md. Pointers are left at each site, but a reader editing a list in place will no longer have the warnings about dollar-signs and quotes directly in front of them — the two mistakes that have previously broken this file.
rollback: git revert the commit. config.sh returns to a single 571-line file, over the cap, and deploy.sh stops pushing the five siblings.

After rollback, run bash -n phone_focus_mode/config.sh, then python3 -m python_pkg.focus_policy --config phone_focus_mode/config.sh | sha256sum and confirm 83e05e82… — the policy must be unchanged in either direction.
A rollback AFTER a deploy leaves five stale config_*.sh files in $REMOTE_DIR. They are inert once config.sh no longer sources them, but remove them so a later audit is not misled.
